summary: C. Peter Bankart works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He has held posts as a Visiting Researcher at Dartmouth College and at Wabash College (attested 2003).

C. Pierce Salguero studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (PhD 2010). A specialist in Buddhist studies and history, he joined Pennsylvania State University as professor in 2010 and became editor-in-chief of Asian Medicine in 2016.

C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College before serving at the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1916 to 1943.
C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932-1933).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980-1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~1992-2020).
Caixi Chen works in Buddhist studies. Chen pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at Presidency University (~1928-1934). Active in Indology and archaeology, he held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935-1946), the Indian Museum (1946), and the Archaeological Survey of India (~1946-1955).

Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Friends Seminary, Harvard (PhD 1959), EPHE, and DIAS. He spent his career as a professor at Harvard University (1959-2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003-2013).

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Bailey studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and Wolfson College, Oxford, completing doctoral work at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Yudru Tsomu. Warner has held academic posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz works in religious studies and Japanology. After earning an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas, Foltz was a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti studied at Milan and completed a PhD at Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Jürgen Hanneder. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he held posts at SOAS, Cambridge, Oxford, the Bodleian Library, and Hamburg.
Carel Gabriel Cobet was a Dutch scholar of linguistics and other fields. He studied at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832-1840), where he later served as a professor (1846, 1849-1884).

Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1958-1960) and Harvard University (~1962-1965), taking up a post at Boston University around 1968.

Carl Bielefeldt studied at UC Berkeley (PhD ~1975-1980) and under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he served on the faculty at Stanford University from around 1980 until retiring as emeritus around 2013.

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Königsberg, and Leipzig (PhD ~1867-1868) under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He completed his habilitation at Jena (~1871-1872) and became a professor there in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from around 1814 to 1816 and later held a post there from around 1820 to 1826.
Carl Darling Buck was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882-1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889-1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, Göttingen, and Helmstedt (PhD). From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor at the University of Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.
Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller, completing his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877.
